When I was in the 4th grade our school went on a over night visit to a Ranch. That night we sat around a campfire and the owner told us scary stories. At the end, our teacher told us if we got scared to let him know to which all the boys scoffed at the idea. Well, I awoke in the middle of the night from a nightmare sitting across from an open window (which freak me out). Our teacher must have heard me because there he was at the side of the bunk bed. He convinced me to go with him to his bunk where he began taking off my clothes. My heart instantly dropped realizing what an idiot I was and that I was in a bad situation. I was too scared to make a sound because, get this, I would have to admit that the whole reason I was in this mess was because I got scared in the first place. At this point, my pajamas were off and I was down to my underwear when, another kid woke up. The teacher went to go check on him and I took this moment to run back to my bed, where I was undisturbed the rest of the night. Never said anything to anyone because of fear of being mocked. That teacher probably molested who knows how many kids.

Sometimes, being a DN is hard. Sure, you travel, sure you wander. But sometimes you run into a place that feels just a little too homey...

For me those places are Salt Lake City, UT, and Siem Reap, Cambodia. both of those cities made me want to settle in for the long haul - in their own way. Both cities were painful to say goodbye to (and get frequent revisiits).

I figured I'd ask /v/digitalnomad ... What place did you have to MAKE yourself leave? What place feels like home to you (besides your actual home city). What places speak to your soul?
For me, it was Crete. Running through the olive trees, hiking the mountains to lagoons, or relaxing beachside. Overwhelmingly, the Greeks we met had never left their own country. We understand why.
